headline: 9 Bangladeshis killed in Kolkata hotel fire
summary: A devastating blaze at a residential hotel near New Market in Kolkata has claimed the lives of nine Bangladeshi nationals, including a child.
details: A massive fire broke out at a residential hotel on Mirza Ghalib Street, near the New Market area of Kolkata, West Bengal.
According to the Kolkata Police and local fire services, nine people, all of whom are Bangladeshi citizens, have died in the incident, including a child.
Eight other individuals were injured in the blaze and are receiving medical treatment.
Preliminary reports suggest the fire may have been caused by an air conditioner explosion, with authorities warning that the death toll could potentially rise.
This tragedy follows another hotel fire in West Bengal over the last two days, where eight people were reported dead in a separate incident.
caption:
9 Bangladeshi nationals, including a child, have been killed in a devastating hotel fire in Kolkata.

A massive fire broke out at a residential hotel on Mirza Ghalib Street, near the New Market area of Kolkata, West Bengal.

According to the Kolkata Police and local fire services, nine people, all of whom are Bangladeshi citizens, have died in the incident, including a child.

Eight other individuals were injured in the blaze and are receiving medical treatment.

Preliminary reports suggest the fire may have been caused by an air conditioner explosion, with authorities warning that the death toll could potentially rise.

This tragedy follows another hotel fire in West Bengal over the last two days, where eight people were reported dead in a separate incident.

headline: Petition filed to stay presidential election after HC order
summary: Supreme Court lawyer Md Eunus Ali Akond has challenged a High Court ruling that cleared the way for the August 20 presidential election.
details: Supreme Court lawyer Md Eunus Ali Akond has filed a petition with the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court seeking a stay on the presidential election scheduled for August 20.
The petition challenges a High Court order that had previously rejected a writ petition seeking to stop the election and questioning the constitutional validity of Article 70.
Article 70 states that a parliamentary seat becomes vacant if a lawmaker resigns from or votes against the political party that nominated them.
The High Court had observed that the presidential election schedule was lawfully announced under the Presidential Election Act, 1991, and found no merit in the challenge.
The HC bench of Justice Khizir Ahmed Choudhury and Justice AFM Saiful Karim noted that any decision regarding Article 70 should be handled by a special parliamentary committee.
Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal previously stated there was no legal bar to holding the election on the scheduled date following the HC ruling.
The original writ petition was filed by Eunus Ali as a public interest litigation on August 13.
caption:
Can the August 20 presidential election be stopped? A new petition has been filed in the Supreme Court to stay the schedule.

Supreme Court lawyer Md Eunus Ali Akond has filed a petition with the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court seeking a stay on the presidential election scheduled for August 20.

The petition challenges a High Court order that had previously rejected a writ petition seeking to stop the election and questioning the constitutional validity of Article 70.

Article 70 states that a parliamentary seat becomes vacant if a lawmaker resigns from or votes against the political party that nominated them.

The High Court had observed that the presidential election schedule was lawfully announced under the Presidential Election Act, 1991, and found no merit in the challenge.

The HC bench of Justice Khizir Ahmed Choudhury and Justice AFM Saiful Karim noted that any decision regarding Article 70 should be handled by a special parliamentary committee.

Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal previously stated there was no legal bar to holding the election on the scheduled date following the HC ruling.

The original writ petition was filed by Eunus Ali as a public interest litigation on August 13.
